title: Flux-gate batcher for hybrid KV streaming
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Streaming chat workloads exhibit wide variance in arrival patterns (microbursts followed by quiet tails). Existing continuous batchers either prioritize latency (inefficient GPU utilization) or throughput (high p99). Additionally, KV cache pressure during long conversations causes GPU memory fragmentation and increased evictions. Goals: 1) Reduce p50/p95 latency regressions for interactive sessions while improving tokens/sec for background/low-priority streams. 2) Avoid KV-slot thrashing and excessive GPU slab fragmentation. 3) Maintain predictable unit cost across mixed-priority traffic. Proposed design: Introduce a "flux-gate" batch formation heuristic that combines (a) a short adaptive time-window, (b) per-session token-budget gating, (c) KV-affinity grouping (co-locate requests likely to hit same KV slots), and (d) GPU-slab-awareness (avoid combining batches that would cause a new slab allocation). Flux-gate computes a per-request flux_score = alpha*arrival_rate_norm + beta*priority_score + gamma*kv_affinity_score - delta*slab_pressure_score. Batch formation rules: - If flux_score >= high_threshold -> immediate micro-batch (low latency). - If flux_score between thresholds -> wait up to window_ms (adaptive; shorter when backend load high). - Otherwise -> accumulate up to token_budget or max_batch_size. KV-affinity: use lightweight locality fingerprinting (last-K-turn hash + slot-range hint) to prefer packing requests with overlapping KV ranges into same batch to reduce duplicate KV reads and improve cache hits. Slab-awareness: runtime exposes a slab_pressure metric per GPU (free_slabs_ratio); flux_score penalizes combinations that would cross the next slab boundary. Trade-offs and tuning knobs: - alpha/beta/gamma/delta are runtime-configurable with sane defaults computed from observed workload percentiles. - Aggressive KV-grouping may slightly increase p50 for low-priority background work but reduces overall GPU memory churn. - Slab-aware restrictions can reduce instantaneous batch size; fallback policy uses a spill-to-worker route when latency SLOs would otherwise be violated. Observability & metrics: experiment tracks p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kv_hit_ratio, slab_allocation_rate, gpu_free_slabs_ratio, and cost_per_1M_tokens. Success criteria: 5-10% improvement in tokens/sec for mixed traffic, <=5% regression in p50 for interactive sessions, 15-30% reduction in slab allocation rate under long conversations. Implementation plan: 1) Prototype flux_score computation in batcher simulation harness (2 weeks). 2) Implement lightweight KV fingerprinting and slab-aware checks in runtime (3 weeks). 3) Canary rollout behind a runtime feature flag, compare against baseline with A/B traffic split (2 weeks). 4) Iterate knobs and document recommended profiles for hosted vs dedicated deployments. Backwards compatibility: flux-gate defaults to tolerant mode (minimal slab checks) and can be fully disabled via config to restore legacy batching behavior.
comments: 2026-02-20 — Triage: Found repeated p99 spikes correlated with slab allocations during long-chat sessions. Assigned to Liam for design + prototype.
2026-02-24 — Design note: Chose locality fingerprinting over full KV index lookup to keep decision path O(1). Logged trade-offs: small probability of suboptimal grouping vs cost of metadata lookup.

2026-03-02 — Engineering update: Prototype implemented in local batcher simulator. Ran mixed-synthetic workload (60% interactive, 40% async). Observed 22% reduction in slab_allocation_rate and 8% increase in tokens/sec, but p95 increased 3% for interactive samples.
2026-03-05 — PM feedback (Rui Chen): Ensure we expose per-customer tuning and an escape hatch for strict latency customers (dedicated). Add labels for host vs dedicated default profiles.
2026-03-07 — Design review (Maya Singh): UX for console should surface flux_score distribution and slab pressure heatmap. Added dashboard link in artifacts.

2026-03-10 — Benchmarking: Canary on a small pool (10 GPUs) with real traffic replayed from last week's production trace. Preliminary results: p50 stable, p95 down 1.5%, slab_allocation_rate down 28%, KV_hit_ratio up 6%. Next: expand canary and iterate thresholds.

2026-03-11 — Blocker note: Observed rare scenario where aggressive KV-affinity groups large long-running conversations causing cold-start latency for other short sessions. Proposed mitigation: preemptive small-batch windows for sessions flagged as interactive; added to follow-up tasks.

Follow-ups: - Add adaptive decay to kv_affinity_score to avoid permanent pinning. - Add a telemetry tag for batches that hit slab boundary to investigate root causes. - Draft runtime flagging API to expose flux parameters for Dedicated customers.
